title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: GYG Persons
tiers.description: Each director of GYG, the Co-Chief Executive Officers, the Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary, Key Management Personnel and persons the Board designates, plus franchisees and restaurant managers and any other person the Board designates in writing; also includes a company or trust controlled by any of these persons.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Management
tiers.description: Each director of GYG, the Co-Chief Executive Officers, the Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary of GYG, Key Management Personnel and persons the Board decides from time to time; distinguished for the obligation to obtain prior consent to trade outside a Blackout Period and to notify the Company Secretary after trading.

tiers.name: all other employees of GYG
tiers.description: Employees who are not GYG Persons; subject to insider trading rules, Blackout Periods, exceptional circumstances relief, protection arrangements/security-and-margin-lending rules and exemptions, but not expressed to be subject to the section 6 consent-to-trade or section 7 post-trade notification obligations.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A spouse (including de facto spouse), child (including step-child or adopted child), a close relative, or a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with a GYG Person, treated as a GYG Person only for the purposes of section 5 (Blackout Periods); a company or trust controlled by a GYG Person is a GYG Person for all purposes of the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any GYG Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including GYG's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any GYG incentive plan) on that GYG Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify 'any other period' as a Blackout Period from time to time (section 5(c)(iv)); the policy does not address whether such additional periods are confidential.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Blanket ban on short-term or speculative trading, including short-term direct dealing and short-term or speculative derivative-market transactions; no numeric holding period is given.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should GYG Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in GYG securities. This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing in GYG securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets ... which are short term or speculative.

transfer GYG securities already held into a self-managed superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary
acquire GYG's ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to GYG's ordinary shares
acquire GYG's securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities managed by that trust provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person

exemption_authority: The Board has absolute discretion to decide what counts as 'exceptional circumstances' (e.g. severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking); the Authorising Officer may then approve, by email, dealings otherwise prohibited (including in a Blackout Period), on confirmation the person holds no Inside Information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GYG Persons and other GYG employees may at any time: ... a disposal of GYG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, GYG expressly permits it 'at any time', including in a Blackout Period, so the bank could enforce against the collared shares on default without putting the executive in breach (subject to post-event notification to the Authorising Officer).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 6 states it 'applies to Directors and Senior Management only', yet its Authorising Officer table (6.1(c)) includes a row for 'Any other GYG Person or other GYG employee', and sections 9.2(b)/9.3(b) (which apply to all GYG Persons and employees) cross-refer to 'consent under paragraph 6.1'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a non-Director/Senior-Management participant the availability of a clearance route for the collar's derivative and security legs is not free of doubt; the conservative reading (and the one supported by the 6.1(c) table) is that Company Secretary/General Counsel consent is still required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which ... operate to limit the economic risk of any GYG Person's security holding ... or otherwise enable a GYG Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is not limited by venue or instrument type, so an OTC put and written call over vested shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and needs consent even though derivatives, hedging and monetisation are not separately named.
There is no floor on retained holdings, so a collar sized against the full vested position would not itself breach a shareholding guideline.

summary: A funded OTC collar is workable once the GYG shares have vested and are free of any holding lock: both the put/call structure (a 'protection arrangement' under 9.2, since it limits economic risk and could profit from a price fall) and the loan secured on the shares (9.3) are permitted with prior consent from the Authorising Officer, taken outside Blackout Periods and while not in possession of Inside Information. Both legs are prohibited outright, with no consent route, while the shares remain unvested or subject to a holding lock. Consent is granted by the Chair of the Board or Audit & Risk Committee chair for directors and senior KMP, and by the Company Secretary or General Counsel for other staff, though the policy's own section headings leave some doubt as to whether non-Director/Senior-Management participants can access this route. A useful feature for the bank is the express carve-out permitting a secured lender's enforcement sale 'at any time', including during a Blackout Period, so default enforcement against the collared shares would not itself breach the policy. There is no minimum shareholding requirement and no defined short-term holding period beyond a general, undated ban on short-term or speculative trading, and the only exemption authority is the Board's case-by-case discretion for hardship or court orders.
